# Cluster Reference

Everything specific to a compute site lives in one folder under `profiles/`. The
config and samplesheet are the same on every cluster; what differs is set once
per cluster, outside git.

## Profiles

A **profile** is a folder under `profiles/` that tells TTpipe how to run jobs
at one compute site. Pick the row that fits you:

| Folder | Use it when | Scheduler |
|--------|-------------|-----------|
| `profiles/slurm-template/` | You have a SLURM cluster of your own. **Start here:** copy it and fill in the `<...>` values ([Set up your own cluster](#own-cluster)) | SLURM |
| `profiles/local/` | You run on one machine, no scheduler ([Single workstation](#workstation)) | none |
| `profiles/biowulf/`, `profiles/longleaf/`, `profiles/pioneer/` | **Examples only.** The template filled in for three real sites (NIH Biowulf, UNC Longleaf, Case Western Pioneer) with the partition names used there (`norm`, `general`, `batch`). Read one as a model; at any other site, make your own profile | SLURM |

The `longleaf` and `pioneer` profiles contain a **required** placeholder,
`slurm_account: <your-slurm-account>`. SLURM rejects submissions until you
replace it with your own account (find it with `sacctmgr show assoc
user=$USER`) or delete the line if your cluster has no accounts. The
`biowulf` profile has no account line. A dry run (`bash TTpipe.sh -n`) does
**not** catch a placeholder left in place: it passes, and the submitted
launcher then fails within a minute with `Failed to evaluate resources value
'<your-slurm-account>'`.

Each folder has two files:

- **`env.sh`**: sourced by `TTpipe.sh` and `unlock.sh`; makes `python3` and
  `conda` available (loads a module, or your own Miniforge).
- **`config.yaml`**: the Snakemake profile: scheduler, account, partition, and each
  rule's threads, memory and time.

A SLURM profile sets `executor: slurm`, `jobs: 100` (at most 100 jobs queued or
running), `latency-wait: 500` (seconds Snakemake waits for files to appear on a
network filesystem), `software-deployment-method: conda`, and
`default-resources` (account, partition, `runtime: 4320` minutes, `mem_mb: 16000`,
`nodes: 1`). The launcher adds `--slurm-logdir <outputDir>/logs_slurm`.

## Choosing the profile

In order: `--profile` on the command line, `$TTPIPE_PROFILE`, then `hpcProfile` in
the config (default `profiles/local`). Set the variable once in `~/.bashrc` and
leave the config alone.

## Environment variables {#environment-variables}

| Variable | Used for | Example |
|----------|----------|---------|
| `TTPIPE_PROFILE` | Which profile folder to use | `profiles/mycluster` |
| `TTPIPE_OUTPUT_ROOT` | Folder a relative `outputDir` goes under (unset: the folder you launch from) | `/data/$USER/ttpipe` |
| `TTPIPE_EMAIL` | Notification address (wins over `notify: email:`) | `you@university.edu` |
| `TTPIPE_CONDA_ROOT` | Where your Miniforge lives, if not `$HOME/miniforge3` | `/data/$USER/miniforge3` |
| `CONDA_PKGS_DIRS` | (a conda variable, not TTpipe's) Where conda caches downloaded packages. The default is inside your Miniforge, usually in `$HOME`; if home has a small quota, environment builds fail with `Disk quota exceeded` (seen on the first real run) | `/scratch/$USER/conda_pkgs` |

```bash
echo 'export TTPIPE_PROFILE=profiles/<cluster>' >> ~/.bashrc
echo 'export TTPIPE_OUTPUT_ROOT=/path/to/scratch/ttpipe' >> ~/.bashrc
source ~/.bashrc
```

If output appears in the folder you launched from, or jobs go to the wrong
partition, the variable was not set in the shell that ran `sbatch`.

## Conda version {#conda-version}

Snakemake 8.27 (pinned in `config/requirements.txt`) needs conda >= 24.7.1. Many
clusters' conda modules are older. Install your own Miniforge once (about 0.5 GB)
and point at it:

```bash
wget https://github.com/conda-forge/miniforge/releases/latest/download/Miniforge3-Linux-x86_64.sh
bash Miniforge3-Linux-x86_64.sh -b -p $HOME/miniforge3
export TTPIPE_CONDA_ROOT=$HOME/miniforge3      # only if it is not $HOME/miniforge3
```

`profiles/biowulf/env.sh` (an example profile) uses `TTPIPE_CONDA_ROOT` if it exists and otherwise `module
load conda`; the others source Miniforge from `TTPIPE_CONDA_ROOT` (default
`$HOME/miniforge3`). Software versions are in `envs/`: Snakemake builds one conda
environment per group of rules on first use (by default into `.snakemake/conda`
where you launch). The environments were solved on one Linux cluster, **not** on
macOS arm64.

## Set up your own cluster {#own-cluster}

For any SLURM cluster, one-time, about ten minutes. SLURM is the job scheduler
many clusters use; commands such as `sinfo` and `sacctmgr` belong to it.

1. **Copy the template** and name it after your cluster:

    ```bash
    cp -r profiles/slurm-template profiles/mycluster
    ```

2. **Find your partition.** A partition is a queue of nodes. List them with
   `sinfo -s` and pick one for ordinary CPU jobs with enough memory per node
   (STAR needs about 26 to 30 GB on a mouse genome and up to about 63 GB to
   build a human index, see below). Your cluster's
   documentation names the right one.
3. **Find your account**, if your cluster uses accounts for billing or
   limits: `sacctmgr show assoc user=$USER format=account%30`. If it prints
   nothing useful, ask your administrators.
4. **Edit `profiles/mycluster/config.yaml`**: set `slurm_partition` and
   `slurm_account` under `default-resources`; delete the `slurm_account` line
   if you have no account. The per-rule numbers below it are starting values.
5. **Set the conda location** in `profiles/mycluster/env.sh`. The template
   uses your own Miniforge at `$HOME/miniforge3` (or `$TTPIPE_CONDA_ROOT`). If
   your site provides conda as a module, `module load ...` here works too, as
   long as conda is 24.7.1 or newer. If your home directory has a small
   quota, see the `Disk quota exceeded` entry in
   [Troubleshooting](troubleshooting.qmd#disk-quota-exceeded-while-building-environments-or-starting-snakemake).
6. **Select the profile** once, in `~/.bashrc`:

    ```bash
    echo 'export TTPIPE_PROFILE=profiles/mycluster' >> ~/.bashrc
    echo 'export TTPIPE_OUTPUT_ROOT=/path/with/space/ttpipe' >> ~/.bashrc
    source ~/.bashrc
    ```

7. **Test with a dry run**, which lists every job and runs nothing, and
   catches most path and config mistakes:

    ```bash
    bash TTpipe.sh -n
    ```

8. **Build the environments, then submit.** Snakemake downloads each conda
   environment on first use, so do the first build on a machine with internet
   access, wait for it to finish, then submit
   ([Building the environments](#building-environments)):

    ```bash
    bash TTpipe.sh --conda-create-envs-only
    sbatch TTpipe.sh
    ```

   Add `sbatch` options such as `--account=...` or `--partition=...` before
   `TTpipe.sh` if your site's defaults do not fit the launcher job.

After a first run, check each job's memory with `seff` or `sacct` and adjust
the profile ([Tuning resources](#tuning-resources)).

::: {.callout-note}
### Example: running on Case Western's Pioneer cluster

This is a worked example for one site, not the only way. Other sites differ in
partition names, scratch locations and quotas; use the steps above and adapt.
The facts here were observed on a real mouse run on Pioneer.

- The `pioneer` profile uses partition `batch`.
- Each user's scratch space is under `/scratch/pioneer/users/<your-username>/`.
- The home-directory quota is small, and conda's package cache sits under the
  Miniforge directory in `$HOME`. Environment builds failed with `Disk quota
  exceeded` until `CONDA_PKGS_DIRS`, `XDG_CACHE_HOME` and `TMPDIR` pointed at
  scratch.
- Miniforge was installed in `$HOME/miniforge3` (the profile's `env.sh` uses
  `TTPIPE_CONDA_ROOT`, default `$HOME/miniforge3`).
- The login node has internet access, and so do the compute nodes (tested:
  conda-forge and PyPI were reachable from a batch job). Building the
  environments on the login node was killed partway in one test, so the
  environments are best built in a SLURM job
  ([Building the environments](#building-environments)).
- A fresh clone has `slurm_account: <your-slurm-account>` in
  `profiles/pioneer/config.yaml`; the launcher fails until you replace it.

```bash
# once, in ~/.bashrc (replace <your-username>)
export TTPIPE_PROFILE=profiles/pioneer
export TTPIPE_OUTPUT_ROOT=/scratch/pioneer/users/<your-username>/ttpipe
export CONDA_PKGS_DIRS=/scratch/pioneer/users/<your-username>/conda_pkgs
export XDG_CACHE_HOME=/scratch/pioneer/users/<your-username>/cache
export TMPDIR=/scratch/pioneer/users/<your-username>/tmp
mkdir -p "$CONDA_PKGS_DIRS" "$XDG_CACHE_HOME" "$TMPDIR"

# find your account, then replace <your-slurm-account> in profiles/pioneer/config.yaml
sacctmgr show assoc user=$USER

# build the conda environments in a job; when it has finished, submit
sbatch --cpus-per-task=8 --mem=32G TTpipe.sh --configfile config/mine.yaml --conda-create-envs-only
sbatch TTpipe.sh --configfile config/mine.yaml
```

`config/mine.yaml` is your complete copy of the config
([Configuration](configuration.qmd)). If your site's default account or
partition does not fit the launcher job, add `--account=<your-slurm-account>`
or `--partition=batch` to the `sbatch` line, before `TTpipe.sh`. The per-rule
memory in `profiles/pioneer/config.yaml` is a starting value. Measured on
mouse, STAR alignment used about 26 GB and the STAR index build about 29 GB
(about 36 minutes). Measured on human (GRCh38 with ERCC92), alignment used
about 29 GB and the index build 62.5 GB (34 minutes on 16 threads), so the
profile's `star_index` memory is now 72000 MB.
:::

## Building the environments {#building-environments}

Snakemake builds one conda environment per group of rules (seven in all) the
first time a rule needs it. Building them all in advance, once, avoids a long
first job and lets you see build failures before anything else runs:

```bash
bash TTpipe.sh --configfile config/mine.yaml --conda-create-envs-only
```

**If your compute nodes have internet access**, run the same command as a SLURM
job instead of on the login node, where long processes may be killed. Pioneer's
compute nodes do; ask your site if you do not know. On Pioneer all seven
environments built in one job in 69 minutes with 8 cores and 32 GB:

```bash
sbatch --cpus-per-task=8 --mem=32G TTpipe.sh --configfile config/mine.yaml --conda-create-envs-only
```

(`snakemake --conda-create-envs-only` with the same profile does the same.) If
the compute nodes have no internet access, build on the login node or another
machine with access
([Troubleshooting](troubleshooting.qmd#the-clusters-compute-nodes-have-no-internet-access)).

**Never run two builds at once**, and do not start the real run while a build
is still going. Overlapping or killed builds that share `.snakemake/conda` and
the package cache left environments with missing standard-library files, and
jobs then failed with `No module named '__future__'` or `Could not find
platform independent libraries`. The fix is to delete the broken environment
folders and the package cache (`CONDA_PKGS_DIRS`) and build once more
([Troubleshooting](troubleshooting.qmd#broken-conda-env)).

## Single workstation {#workstation}

With no scheduler, use `profiles/local` (it is the default, so nothing needs
selecting):

1. Install Miniforge once ([Conda version](#conda-version)); `env.sh` looks
   for it at `$HOME/miniforge3` or `$TTPIPE_CONDA_ROOT`.
2. Know your memory. STAR needs roughly 26 to 30 GB for a mouse genome
   (measured about 26 GB for alignment and 29 GB for the index build); a
   machine with less cannot align it, and there is no setting that avoids
   that. Human measured about 29 GB for alignment and 62.5 GB for the index
   build; other genomes have not been measured.
3. Set the limit in `profiles/local/config.yaml`: `resources: - mem_mb=64000`
   is the total memory TTpipe may use at once. Set it to a little below your
   machine's free memory. Snakemake starts jobs only while their `mem_mb`
   fits, so with `star_align` at 40000 only one alignment runs at a time.
   `cores: all` uses every CPU core.
4. Dry run, then run, from the repository folder:

    ```bash
    bash TTpipe.sh -n
    bash TTpipe.sh
    ```

   Run it inside `screen` or `tmux` (general knowledge) so that closing your
   terminal does not stop it.

## Per-rule resources

Rules carry only `threads:`; the profile's `set-threads` and `set-resources` give
the rest (`mem_mb` in MB, `runtime` in minutes for SLURM). These are the shipped
values. **They are starting guesses chosen from tool documentation and typical
mouse-genome needs, not benchmarks of TTpipe.**

| Rule | Threads | `mem_mb` | `runtime` (min) | Notes |
|------|---------|----------|-----------------|-------|
| `fastqc` | 4 | 4000 | 120 | per sample and mate |
| `fastp` | 8 | 8000 | 120 | only if `trim: true` |
| `star_index` | 16 | 48000 (`pioneer`: 72000) | 240 | only if `build_star_index: true`; mouse measured about 29 GB, human + ERCC 62.5 GB, so raise it for human |
| `star_align` | 16 | 40000 | 480 | per sample; measured about 26 GB on mouse and 29 GB on human |
| `mapq_filter` | 8 | 4000 | 120 | |
| `mark_duplicates` | 2 | 16000 | 240 | Picard; no Java heap is set by the rule |
| `split_strands` | 8 | 8000 | 240 | per sample and strand |
| `merge_bams` | 8 | 8000 | 240 | |
| `scale_factors` | 1 | 2000 | 15 | |
| `bigwig` | 8 | 8000 | 240 | |
| `bigwig_sample` | 8 | 8000 | 240 | only if `sample_tracks: true` |
| `gene_info` | 1 | 2000 | 15 | |
| `htseq_count` | 1 | 8000 | 480 | `--order pos` buffers unmatched mates in memory |
| `count_matrix` | 1 | 4000 | 30 | |
| `sample_table` | 1 | 1000 | 5 | |
| `deseq2` | 2 | 8000 | 60 | |
| `rnk` | 1 | 2000 | 15 | |
| `fgsea` | 2 | 8000 | 120 | |
| `sankey` | 1 | 4000 | 30 | |
| `results_explorer` | 1 | 4000 | 30 | the page grows with contrasts and GSEA collections; raise memory only if the job log shows it |
| `qc_summary` | 1 | 2000 | 15 | |
| `qc_report` | 2 | 8000 | 30 | |
| `multiqc` | 1 | 4000 | 30 | |

The `local` profile has no `runtime`; it sets `cores: all`, `latency-wait: 60` and a
global `resources: mem_mb=64000`.

## Tuning resources {#tuning-resources}

1. **Look at what a first run used.** For SLURM jobs: `seff <jobid>` or `sacct -j
   <jobid> --format=JobID,JobName,MaxRSS,Elapsed,State`. Snakemake also writes a
   benchmark table per job (`<sample>/benchmarks/<rule>.tsv` or
   `benchmarks/<rule>.tsv`) with wall time and peak memory (`max_rss`, in MB).
2. **Edit the profile**, not the rule: raise `mem_mb` or `runtime` for the rule
   that was killed (`OUT_OF_MEMORY` or `TIMEOUT` in `sacct`). Keep a margin.
3. **Threads** come from `set-threads`. More threads help STAR, the samtools steps
   and `bamCoverage`; HTSeq, DESeq2's single job and the others gain little. A rule
   asking for more threads than your partition's nodes offer will not be scheduled.
4. **Resubmit.** Finished jobs are kept; only the failed ones rerun.

With the `local` profile the global `mem_mb=64000` limits how many jobs run at
once. With `star_align` at 40000, only one STAR job fits at a time; lower the
numbers or raise the limit to match your machine. A laptop with less memory than a
STAR alignment needs cannot align a mouse genome.

## Email

`TTPIPE_EMAIL` and `notify:` in the config send three workflow emails (start,
finish, failure). SLURM's own mail about the launcher job is separate:
`sbatch --mail-user=$TTPIPE_EMAIL TTpipe.sh` (the header already sets
`--mail-type=END,FAIL,TIME_LIMIT_80`). Check that your cluster can send mail:
`echo test | mail -s test $TTPIPE_EMAIL`.
